title: Measuring Recommender System Effects with Simulated Users
reasoning: The paper was presented at the 'Workshop on Fairness, Accountability, Transparency, Ethics and Society on the Web (FATES)'. It proposes a simulation framework specifically designed to measure and understand the effects of recommender systems, with a strong focus on biases like popularity bias and filter bubbles. The motivation is explicitly ethical, aiming to answer questions like whether a system fosters unhealthy habits. This framework serves as a tool for auditing the ethical implications and fairness of recommender systems, thus having a core component of evaluating system ethics.
